restatement.intent: Give a vision model pictures only for the judgement that vision is good at, and deliver every position, size and score as a row of numbers carrying a stable id. Pictures label items with those same ids, pack many items into one sheet, and are rationed by a budget the agent knows about.
restatement.problem: When an agent must both see and measure, pictures alone give it imprecise numbers and an unbounded image count, while numbers alone leave it unable to judge what they describe.
restatement.solution: Split the work: a measurement produces item rows (id, position, size, scores) and those numbers are the only source of measurement the agent may use. Pictures exist to support judgement only — each item drawn and labelled with its row id, many items to a sheet of small magnified cells, several views per cell where the decision needs them. Never let the agent read a number off a picture; it answers by id and the engine maps ids back to exact rows. A stated per-call and per-conversation budget caps pictures, and omitted pictures are named in a warning instead of vanishing.

quiz.answer: Because contrast varies between cells: under one shared stretch a faint item is washed out next to a bright one, so each cell gets its own range (`stretch: "cell"`) and both remain judgeable in the same sheet.

They are not delivered; each one is named in a `LOOKS` warning giving its label and line, plus a generic fix hint (fewer cells per sheet, smaller zoom). Budget overflow becomes an actionable warning rather than a silently dropped picture or a rejected run.
quiz.where: Implementation notes (7); Sketch, `deliver`; Consequences (+) Budget failures become warnings

quiz.answer: Because APIs downscale large images before the model sees them, which erases small features (three-pixel specks). A sheet carries many small crops that are each magnified, so detail survives the downscale in one image; an uncropped overview is not the same thing and loses the detail.
quiz.where: Implementation notes (8) and (3); Forces (Context against detail)

quiz.answer: The scene and a band-pass ("speck") view of the same cell: the scene shows what the object is, the band-pass shows whether it stands out from grain.
quiz.where: Implementation notes (4); Solution, "several views side by side"

transfer.why: It is close to an isomorphism of the dust case: a measurement (the detector) already produces candidates with ids, geometry and scores, and the model's job is visual confirmation, not measurement. Only the number of candidates (40) exceeds what fits in one sheet, which is exactly what the budget half of the pattern is for.

participants.Item rows: Detector output per scan: id, centroid x/y, slice index z, effective diameter in mm, mean/variance HU, detector score — exact and citable.
participants.Marked view: One annotated axial slice with a numbered circle per candidate, for judging spatial context (near pleura, near hilum) when only a few candidates matter.
participants.Sheet: Grid of magnified crops, one cell per candidate, each cell showing two windowings side by side and labelled with the row id; ~12–15 cells per sheet, so 40 candidates is three sheets.
participants.View presets: Lung window (nodule vs parenchyma), mediastinal/soft-tissue window (vessel vs node, calcification), optionally a sharpened/edge view; plus adjacent slices as separate views.
participants.Budget: Per call: at most 2 sheets; per conversation: e.g. 6 sheets, stated in the agent's instructions so it can plan 40 candidates over three calls instead of discovering the limit on rejection.
participants.Deliverer: Attaches the sheets generated by a call in order up to the limits and names each omitted sheet by line in a `LOOKS` warning.

transfer.sketch:
value Item: id, cx, cy, z, r_mm, hu, score          -- from the detector, exact

cands = detect(nodules(scan))                            -- ~40 rows, ids stable
keep  = sortBy(cands, -score)[0:12]                      -- agent filters in code
sheet(keep, views: [window("lung"), window("mediastinal")],
      cell: 64 px, zoom: 2, stretch: "cell").look("top 12")
-- repeat on the next 12 rows; three sheets cover the scan, six is the session cap

deliver(callPictures, budget) → (delivered, warnings)    -- unchanged from the chapter

byId = { i.id: i for i in keep }
for i in answer.nodules:
  if i not in byId: return refuse(E_UNKNOWN_ID, i, valid: keys(byId),
                                  hint: "cite ids from the last sheet")
labels = [byId[i] for i in answer.nodules]               -- exact cx, cy, z, r_mm
key_notes: (1) Diameters, HU and slice positions must come from rows and never be read off the crop — a grid or ruler here would produce clinically wrong measurements.
(2) Ids must be the detector's ids, not 1..12 by sheet position: the agent filters 40 down to 12 and may answer across several sheets, which relabelling breaks immediately.

(3) The ~15-cell cap forces three sheets for 40 candidates — size the per-call and per-conversation budget around that, and shrink cell size only after checking a known-size nodule still reads after downscaling.
(4) Two views side by side is what makes the judgement: lung window for what the opacity is, mediastinal window to separate a vessel or node from a nodule.
(5) Per-cell stretch matters because a ground-glass nodule next to a dense calcified one disappears under a shared range.
(9) Refuse ids not on the sheet the agent actually saw; this is a safety-relevant answer path, so unknown or stale ids should be errors, not guesses.
transfer.risk: One axial crop per cell makes a vessel seen in cross-section look exactly like a nodule (it disappears on adjacent slices), and cramming all 40 candidates into one sheet drops each cell below the size that survives API downscaling — so the model confidently confirms artefacts. Correct shape: 12–15 cells per sheet, with the adjacent slices or the second windowing as the per-item view that defeats the vessel look-alike.

transfer.why: There is nothing to number: a colour cast is a property of the whole frame, not of items with identity or position, and the chapter's own Do-not-use clause names "a global colour cast" as the counter-case. Marks and sheets would also mislead — a cell-wise stretch would destroy exactly the cross-photo comparability the task needs.

participants.Budget: still useful but trivial — one picture per photo, so ten images, checked against the transport cap
participants.Deliverer: still useful — warn by line if a photo cannot be delivered
participants.Item rows: does not apply: no items; the measurable numbers are per-photo channel means / neutral-patch readings, not per-item rows
participants.Marked view / Sheet / View presets: do not apply: any marking or cropping removes the whole-frame colour context the judgment depends on

key_notes: Only the budget and deliverer halves survive; the marks, sheets and per-cell stretch are actively harmful here.
If anything numeric is wanted, this is the "Numbers only" variation: per-photo channel means and grey-patch offsets, with one unstretched picture per photo as confirmation.
transfer.risk: Numbered marks and sheets give the illusion of the pattern while destroying the property being judged: per-cell stretching makes each photo internally consistent and so hides the very cast differences between photos the white-balance correction depends on.

review_notes.note: The headline evidence is weaker than the prose implies: "two pi agents… located 14 and 13 of 53… against 4 and 5" is n=2 per arm, and the very next sentence reports "both versions located 9 of 13" in annotator-style sessions. A reader can conclude the pattern only helped on the question task, and the chapter does not explain why the two tasks differ.
review_notes.suggestion: Separate the claims: what the pattern reliably fixed (precision of reported positions — false positives fell from 15/12 to 2/5) versus mixed recall results; give run counts and say which task shape each number came from.

review_notes.note: The 24-of-32 and 15/12 numbers describe items the measurement never found — the sheet-only design cannot recover them, because a sheet can only show candidates the measurement produced, and the chapter offers no recall fallback. The Consequences bullet ("things no measurement finds will not be in any sheet") states the hole but the Solution and Variations never close it.
review_notes.suggestion: Add a variation for recall: one unmarked overview or lettered-grid sheet per region/tile alongside the marked sheets, or the "Labelled grid instead of item marks" variation explicitly framed as the recall pass before candidates exist.

review_notes.note: "Marked view" (a picture where "each item is drawn and labelled") and "Sheet" ("a grid of small cells, one per item, each… labelled by id") overlap: a sheet is also a picture with items marked and labelled. The Collaboration steps only ever use a sheet, so the reader cannot tell when to use a single marked view instead.
review_notes.suggestion: Define the split by purpose and cost: marked view = one whole scene with all items marked, for spatial relationships among few items, one image; sheet = crops of many items, the only way to keep detail past downscaling. Say which one the dust runs used for which decision.

review_notes.note: "An agent may cite an id it was never shown, or one from an earlier sheet… refuse unknown ids" merges two different cases. Refusing an id the agent legitimately saw on an earlier, still-valid sheet throws away a correct answer, and on a 40-candidate scan with three sheets that will happen constantly.
review_notes.suggestion: Distinguish `E_UNKNOWN_ID` from `E_STALE_ID` in the `refuse` kind, and give stale ids a fix that re-displays the sheet (or resolves them against the session's live row set) instead of an error.

review_notes.note: The `deliver` pseudocode does not match its own description. The per-conversation term is written `session.picturesSoFar < budget.perConversation`, mixing a count against a limit name; bytes are only checked after the per-call count; and nothing says whether `warnings` reach the agent (as text in the reply) or are logged for the operator.
review_notes.suggestion: Use `budget.perConversationCount` and `session.picturesSoFar < budget.perConversationCount`, decide and state the precedence of the three checks explicitly, and say that warnings are appended to the reply the agent reads.

review_notes.section: Problem / Solution vs Forces (Delivery against attention)
review_notes.note: Concrete limits are scattered with no explanation of what determines them: 100 / 50 / 4 pictures / 8 MiB / 12–15 cells / 40 px / zoom 4. A reader with a different API or feature size has to guess which are principles and which are goja-cv constants.
review_notes.suggestion: One short "tuning" paragraph: cells per sheet ≈ how many cells keep a feature above N pixels after the API's known downscale (verify with a test feature of known size); bytes cap from the transport; cells per call from a fixed 2×6 layout. Mark the rest as goja-cv defaults.

review_notes.note: "the 39-agent study" and "the pi subagents handbook records the same finding" are cited as load-bearing evidence but cannot be identified or checked. The same applies to the tool-call counts (223 / 161 / 153) about which helpers agents actually use.
review_notes.suggestion: Name the study and the handbook entry (file or section), or drop the numbers; note 10's conclusion — put evidence tools in the helpers and examples agents copy — is worth keeping even without the counts.

review_notes.note: The Solution paragraph is one long run-on that repeats all five participants plus the budget rule, and the Motivation's four "also appears elsewhere" bullets repeat the Applicability list almost word for word. "View presets" appears as a participant but never in the Collaborations, so it reads as configuration dressed as a participant.
review_notes.suggestion: Cut the Solution to two sentences (numbers carry measurement; marked, budgeted pictures carry judgement) and let the Structure table carry the participants; reduce the Motivation bullets to one line each or delete them; either rename "View presets" a configuration or give it a collaboration step.

ratings.comment: The core rule (numbers for measuring, ids for pointing, sheets for seeing, a stated budget) is memorable and transferred almost mechanically to the CT case, but the marked-view/sheet overlap, the sloppy deliverer pseudocode and the unsourced evidence keep it from being cleanly reusable as written.
